newsitem.title: USA: Lott says U.S. gas tax action unlikely this week.
newsitem.headline: Lott says U.S. gas tax action unlikely this week.

text.p: Senate Majority Leader Trent Lott said he did not think Congress would have time this session to act on legislation earmarking the receipts from a 4.3-cents-per-gallon gas tax to the federal highway trust fund.

"I just don't see right now how we have time to do that," Lott said. He said discussions were continuing with lawmakers, but was not hopeful Congress would be able to act on the issue before adjourning at the end of this week or early next week.
"I don't see how we can actually get that done in the last week," he said.

Lott also said Republican leaders were continuing to work with the White House to craft a omnibus spending bill to fund government agencies in 1997. Lott said he still expected final action before the new fiscal year begins on Oct 1, but did not know the timing of the measure.
He warned that the Senate might have to be in session over the weekend to complete action on the measure. Lott also said a broad measure to revamp U.S. immigration laws might be added to the measure.
